dialogue.text: Oh, phew! Oh, right, they can swim. It's all coming back to me now.
Bender! Romance isn't about money.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Oh, so it's just coincidence that Zoidberg here is desperately poor and miserably lonely? Puh-lease!
Doesn't it bother you even a little to be taking advantage of your girlfriend's trust?

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Oh, wait, you're serious. Let me laugh even harder.
Well, at least you saved us from, uh, you. Thank God you finally overcame your incompatibility with Robot 1-X.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Oh, yeah, we were totally in sync! I was like "Save them!" and he was all "No problem!" and then he did it--
Aren't you upset at all? How would you feel if I flushed Fry down the toilet?

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Only one way to find out.
Oh, no, not at all. If anything, I'm more impressed.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Ooh! I'm gonna need to make some room.
I met him at that charity cock fight last week. He's the mayor's aide.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Ooh! You go, mutant girl!
Nice ass, ass.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Ooh, sparks! Buy her a rose, I guarantee she'll put out!
Wow! The burial chamber of the 20th century's greatest spiritual leader, Al Sharpton.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Ooh. Now this guy had taste!
What? Are you talking? Oh, God! I'm deaf!

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Oops. I'm so, so sorry, Leela. I just wanted to annoy you.
No, I mean cool your jets. They're melting Bender's face.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Ow! Oh, my God! Ow!
Nevvveeeeer!

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: People, I'm sorry. You've never before heard me say those words, or even the individual letters that make them up. But I am. And with a huge amount of modesty, I humbly beg your forgiveness.
You know I hate lying. But those orphans were so proud of me, I couldn't bear to let them down.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Pfff! At least Reverend Pickens had the dignity to jump out the whorehouse window with his pants around his ankles.
I'm taking this bee with us. With a queen we can build a hive and make more honey ourselves. Let me just pack her a lunch and we'll go.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Pick up the pace, lady! I'm sick of shaking my booty for these fat jerks. I didn't mean you're all fat. Just fatso there.
Well, Fry's opera premiere's tomorrow night. I'm off to find a pair of formal gloves that'll fit over my enormous forearms.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Pretty annoying, huh, Leela?
Ugh! Great. We're two days from Earth with no food.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Problem solved You two fight to the death and I'll cook the loser. Work his gut; I like it tender.
You guys distract the were-car and I'll kill it by plugging its exhaust pipe with this silver potato.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Psst, there it is.
Since when are you my agent?

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Quiet, call coming in. Yes? A big endorsement deal for Leela? How much? Hey! You put a one and two zeroes in front of that or we pass! Deal!
Look at this. They found those same rubbery tracks right here in New New York. There was a hit-and-run by the robot porno theatre.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Robot porno theatre? I was in that... general area last night. Whoever ran me down out on the moors must've followed me back here.
OK, thanks, Bender. Let's fan out and look for him.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Roger that, I got a map of the ship right here.
What are you doing to my ship?

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Sanctifying it! There! That ought to convert a few tailgaters.
Bender, shush. You're supposed to be dead.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Say more about how great I am. And where's the crying? You people look like you're waiting for the bus.
Says who?

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Says the only human whose opinion I even remotely respect. Inspector 5, the best inspector a kid could want. The day I was built, he looked me over, probably with tears of pride in his eyes, and proclaimed to all the world, by means of this scrap of paper, that I was perfect and infallible in every way!
How was the wedding, Bender?

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Says who?! I didn't witness anything!
Just deliver the package and let's get outta here.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Screw that! I ain't no delivery boy! I'm the company's chef.
Well, I wouldn't mind rubbing my success in a few choice faces.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Set a course for adventure!
Does that mean they only do 60% of the work you do or that they actually do more work because they're only 60% as lazy?

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Shut up. That's a good one.
We made it! And some of the animals survived.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: So a couple of animals didn't die and Leela got lucky. That's what I call a successful mission!
Just make a simple cake. And this time, if someone's going to jump out of it, make sure you put them in after you cook it.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: So it's a cake you want, is it? I'll make you a cake you'll never forget.
Ooh! Was it jazz noodling? My ex-boyfriend Sean played the sax. I used to listen for hours while he sat naked on my couch and improvised.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: So musicians really Rodger your Hammerstein, huh?
Nothing.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: So should we get our stuff and head down to the planet?
I don't believe it! It's dark matter.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: So this guy just unloaded a steaming pile of starship fuel?
Nothing. We just talked.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: So what's your problem? It's not like you slept with him. Oh, my God!
Fry, he opened up relations with China. He doesn't want to hear about your ding-dong.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: So, Nixon. Even if you miss your body, being a head's great too, right?
Oh, uh, hey, Fry!

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: So, as Leela was saying, Fry can go shove a big, old-- Ow!
Hello, there. Hmm. He doesn't seem to be on the checklist.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: So, you're saying we can cook him?
But it's doing long-term damage to the planet.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: So? It's not like it's the only one we've got.
What the hell happened?

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Some breaking occurred, the dolly was involved, that's about all we know.
Bender, what happened?

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Somebody tried to run me over. And not with a normal hover-car. It crept along the ground on round, rubber feet, like a wolf!
Bummer.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Someone fat get in my way! I'm broken again. I can't move any part of me.
This is all a big load. I was the one trying to save the Popplers. You were sucking them down like the fat hog you are and you were stepping on them for fun. You both should be in here instead of me.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Someone's acting awfully aluminum.
Me? Perfectly normal?

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Sons, daughters, meet Uncle Fry.
Well rot in peace. Fry and I are leaving.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Sorry, but we're totally sealed in. Nothing can get in or out. Except millions of snakes. Here, have a pomegranate schnapps from my private distillery and start sharing fond memories of me, Bender.
The Mona Lisa!

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Sorry, it's not quite finished.
Hey! He stole my ring!

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Sorry. Well, that solves the mystery of the missing ring. This calls for a drink.
She doesn't really love you. She can't. She's just a machine that--

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Stay away from our women! You got metal fever, boy! Metal fever!
I didn't create anything. I stole it.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Stealin' is a form of creativity!
Let's see what you got. Touch your toes.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Still... can't... reach!
No. But I bet it wasn't someone who was good at stealing.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Stop it, stop it! It's not right! You've crossed a line.
Also, if our identities get out, every crook in the city will be after us. Or, God forbid, our loved ones.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Superking has no need for loved ones. How ya doin', kid?
No! Everything's just--

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Sure is shocking about the Professor, huh?. And now Hermes is mysteriously missing. Anyhow, it doesn't affect me, Bender. Hey, what's this? Hermes' dreadlocks? And his arm? Leela, I'm shocked. Food goes in the disposal, hair and flesh go in the trash!
There. Good as new! Except we're three miles below the surface, we don't have any food and the ship won't work underwater.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Tempers are wearing thin. Let's just hope some robot doesn't kill everybody.
Bender, he's got your body!

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: That dirty, double-crossing bastard! How dare he run off with Richard Nixon!
What is it?

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: That painting, the eyes are watching me!
Thank you all for the inspiring advice, but I'm perfectly happy with my life the way it is.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: That sounds like a cry for help.
No, over here! Flying saucer captured!

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: That's no flying saucer! That's my ass!
Professor, We need to talk to you about Fry.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: That's right, we want some money— Wait. What's this about Fry?
They're so lifeless-like.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: That's the world's greatest robot artist, Vincent van Gobot. He was built without an ear, but then he went crazy and had one installed.
You are one devious bastard.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: That's what it says on my vanity plate.
Bender, dating your co-worker and primary mode of transportation is immoral, illogical and a violation of interstellar shipping statute 437-B.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: That's what makes it so nasty!
Bender, damage report.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: The auxiliary power's out, and they spilled my cocktail.
You recorded that?

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: The eyePhone records everything. All I did was add a laugh track and twit it to my 10,000 followers.
This is unbelievable. The old Bender never would have taken us out to dinner.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: The old Bender's gone. He won't trouble you anymore.
and In marriage.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: The use of words expressing something other than their literal intention, Now that is "irony".
Alright, Liu. Time to kick your frosty, well-toned ass! Yah!

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Then along came Bender.
Kind of fatty.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Then how about this little number? Pure-bred human. No vampire in there.
Forty kilometers. Fifty!

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: There must be petroleum oil down here somewhere. Go deeper! Deeper!
Let's see. If that's Hypodermic Ridge then the bomb must go right here. Get ready to run. We've got 25 minutes. Uh, 15 minutes. 5 minutes. "6h" minutes?

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: There's your problem. The Professor put the counter on upside-down.
OK, crew, listen up. Your job is to delivery these 40 pillows to that hotel.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: They're not very heavy but you don't hear me not complaining.
We haven't thought of a name yet.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: They're tasty, right? Let's call 'em "Tasty-cles".
Completely out of ice?

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: This could mean the end of the banana daiquiri as we know it... also life.
Bender, four and a half weeks of oil wrestling sounds like plenty.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: This isn't a lousy reform Robanukah! We need more petroleum oil!
Hey, Bender, look at that woman's purse. It's hanging by a spaghetti strand.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Thou shalt not snatch.
Look, I agree that it makes space walking more comfortable, but, for a photo shoot, it's a little... Unsavoury. Over.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Time is money, peaches. Now shut your com link and make love to the camera. And remember I'm the camera. Stop actually washin' and play with the sponges!
I'm zeroing in on him. BENGAY... mothballs... letters to the editor. It's the Professor!

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: To the flying machine!
After a whole life of searching, I may finally have found where I belong.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Too bad it's a dump.
No! You didn't! You just corralled a bunch of stiffs at the bus station and pocketed our money!

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: True. But in the end, isn't that what Valentine's Day is really all about?
What?

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: True. I've always dreamt of being an emperor. You know, for Halloween, and then forever. But heisting those jewels would be difficult.
They are now. In the 2600's, New Yorkers elected a super-villain governor, and he stole most of the world's monuments.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Truly a great man. Look at him up there.
Fine. You'll get your cut. I don't really care about the money, anyway. I just wanna show those poor, disadvantaged orphans that they can succeed in life.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Ugh. You are the worst kind of rich person.
Bender, quick! Waggle something!

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Uh... Hello, fellow bees. How's the abdomen? Swollen with nectar, I trust?
The exit! We made it.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Uh, Your Majesty, I brought the prisoners.
Oh, I completely forgot. I left my apartment on fire!

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Uh, as for me, I'm late for my LSAT's.
Steady, Planet Express Ship. Focus on diverting all power to the scramjets.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Uh, look, Planet Express Ship, this might not be the best time, but, well, I really like you and whatever, but, I think we should just be friends.
But the ship is dirty.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Uh, whatever. I ran out of film an hour ago.
This coming-together of superstars really means a lot to you, doesn't it, Bender?

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Uh-huh. Helping my defective brothers is the first thing I've ever cared about, even the slightest bit. You know, when I first got broken, I thought my life was over. But look at me now I've got fame, money, groupies, and it's all thanks to being completely immobilised. That's why I'll be proud to go up on stage tomorrow and say, "Look at me, world, I am a broken robot!".
Am I under arrest?

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Wait! I know you. You're the sleazebag who owns the Ultimate Robot Fighting League.
Bender, stop trying to destroy the world.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Wait, wait, wait, wait. Is it "sorry"? No. "Fun-derful"? Uh, "non-alcoholic"?
I don't know why I should. I mean after what he--

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Wait, wait, wait, wait. What is it you like best about me?
Bender! How could you be so lazy and irresponsible?

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Wait, what? Did someone say I'm great?
Let's just say we've "crossed paths".

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Was that before or after you slept with him?
Yes. My parents were so hurt, I couldn't help it! But I distinctly told them not to tell anyone.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: We are not amused.
We've got to go back in toime an' set things straight! 'Urry up an' lick Washin'ton's 'ead again!

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: We can't! There's no George Washington nor any other Presidents.
Since when do you care about us?

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: We thought you only cared about cans of anchovies and stuffy old songs about the buttocks.
Although he is completely right.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: We've got to stem this tidal wave of moral decay. It's time to shut down nappster.com!
Aw! They love you!

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Well I don't love them. Aw! I don't know why but when I look down at their little faces, it makes me wanna puke! In a good way!
This is the first actual work you've ever had to do around here.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Well I'm not doing it! It's a robot holiday.
I can't make out a thing!

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Well, I guess you should've had two eyes!
Really?

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Well, it's 30 bucks, and there's a $10-mail-in rebate. When the League of Robots hears about this, they won't be pleased. Oh, you'll pay, my darlings.
No I don't. But I think we ought to meet with him and see if he'll help us rescue those animals.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Well, just in case you guys hit it off, you'll wanna take this with you.
Then we have no choice. We'll have to mercy-kill the Professor ourselves.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Well, let's get started.
I guess not.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Well, the doomsday device is ready. Maybe blasting this quadrant of space into a hell storm of flaming nothingness will cheer me up a little.
This will make a great episode. But talk slower. I can't type that fast.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Well, well, well. You didn't make up that TV show! You just wrote down what these space twerps said!
Hi, Bender. We'd like to adopt a child.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Well, you've come to the right place because Honest Bender's Orphanarium means discount orphans. Now, little lady. What do I have to do to send you home with 12 orphans today?
Lars asked me out!

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: What are you doing, wonderful masters?
Eg, it's putrid! What do you feed him?

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: What comes out one end we feed to the other. Also Indian food. Let the contest begin!
Nightfall's coming. Hurry, before we freeze.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: What do you mean "we", mammal?
Bender! You're three hours late. You can't give up on your training now after both of us worked so hard.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: What do you mean, "we"?
Careful with that doomsday device, Bender.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: What does it matter? I'll never be a Globetrotter. My life, and, by extension, everyone else's, is meaningless.
Wow. This is beautiful.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: What's with all the crap?
Bender, you need to go to the police and tell them a tastefully edited version of what you just said.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: What, and have the Mafia come after me too?! No way! This secret goes to my grave!
Until she sneaks out!

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: When I grow up, I wanna be a steam shovel!
You call that a wound? That's a boo-boo tops. But thanks for trying to save me, Fry. Fry?! He's... he's dead!

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Who will make Bender waffles just the way he likes them now?
That's me over in Cootietown.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Whoa! Get a load of this average-looking guy!
Gentlemen, I've completed my report on the crash.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Whoa! I'm not reading that crap. Summarise it in one word.
Bender, it's OK to be proud but don't be a show-off.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Whoa! You look a lot better than you used to for some reason.
Well, you heard the windbag We've been drafted. Everyone into the ship.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Whoa, whoa, whoa, whoa, hold on. I refuse to fight. I'm a conscientious objector.
The magician?

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Whoa, whoa, whoa. Wouldn't it take millions of years to evolve into mermaids?
OK, Fnog, that's enough. Call him off. Fnog? Hmm.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Why won't anyone help me?
We're cutting through the Bermuda Tetrahedron.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Woo! Wait. The Bermuda Tetrahedron?
I guess everything worked out jolly oll right, eh, guv'nor?

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Wot's with th' fruity accent, ducky? Bollocks! Ah've got it, too!
There. No rampaging for you tonight.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Wouldn't it make sense to weld everyone except me to the wall?
Actually, the space whale isn't a space fish. It's a space mammal.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Wow, interesting. I'm both impressed and being eaten.
That's not true.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Xmas tree, oh, Xmas tree! Bah-boo-bee-boo-bah-bee-boh.
We recycle everything. Robots are made from old beer cans.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Yeah! And this beer can is made outta old robots.
But we're your friends and we live here in the year 3000.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Yeah! Now are you gonna come to the squid fights with us or sit here wallowing in your prehistoric junk?
Wait a minute. Why aren't you gonna kill us anymore?

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Yeah! What are you chicken?
But the phoney stuff is what's fun. It's boring out there.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Yeah! You're the kind of guy who visits Jerusalem and doesn't want to see the Sexeteria!
Prepare for lift-off. We're out of fuel. Bender, I told you to fill the tank before we left.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Yeah, I'll do it when we get back.
Please, Professor. Give us our jobs back. We deserve another chance.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Yeah, and if you won't give me another chance, perhaps you'd give one to... Og, gorilla emperor of Earth!
We did it! We won!

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Yeah, but it'll never bring back my martini. Well, who wants a martini?
You're just saying that because he bought you that antique robot toy.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Yeah, it is cute.
Well, at least it'll help reduce their population.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Yeah, life is hilariously cruel. Permission to come aboard, Wiggles?
We sure are cheerful this morning.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Yeah, this past week with Fry's been a blast! Y'know, beneath this warm, sunny exterior beats the cold, mechanical heart of a robot.
And not one of those bogus everyday miracles like a sunrise. Aren't you a male?

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Yeah, what's the deal? Just when I thought I'd figured out you biological creatures, it's something else! Lemme at 'im! Come over here, Kif! You--
But it's set 800 years in the past!

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Yeah, why is this so important to you?
I kind of hoped this whole experience would have left you a little more open to your sensitive side.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Yeah, you'd think, but what you gonna do?
It's funny how the battle of the sexes was only resolved when a Manbot and a Fembot realised they loved each other.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Yeah. By the way, if she calls, I'm not here. All I know is this gold says that was the best mission ever!
You do?

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Yeah. I mean, one cantaloupe-sized bloodshot eye? You ain't winning no beauty pageants, lady.
Oh, they're all so adorable.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Yeah. You know, it's times like this I can hardly bear to let them go. Goodnight, you princes of Maine, you kings of New New England.
Mmm. The ingredients are cooked. And they've picked up some of your natural robot flavourings. Time to add the yeast.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Yeast? You mean I'll have a lifeform growing inside me? It's so beautiful.
Anytime. I actually enjoyed hanging out with you.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Yep, everything worked out great thanks to good old Bender.
They used to be such peaceful birds. I suppose this was your doing.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Yep. It's like I taught 'em If it ain't black and white, peck scratch and bite! Now to take off my tuxedo. Guys, it's me! Your lovable dictator! Uh-oh!
Of course not. In fact, he's a crook.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Yep. Stolen Pez anyone?
OK Bender, we're here. It's time to get to work.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Yes Miss Leela, tote that space barge, lift that space bale.
Wait! Take me first!

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Yes! Take her first.
So Flexo and Angle-ine had sex right there on the factory floor? Well, at least you got bending out of your system.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Yes. I won't be up to bending again for a long, long time.
Come on, before it's too late!

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: You all go without me. I'm gonna take one last look around. You know, for, uh, stuff to steal.
That's what makes it so sad. I thought I was doing something heroic.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: You are. What about that little girl you visited in the hospital? You know the one I mean? The one who died?
I asked you five minutes ago.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: You call that a kiss? I'll show you! C'mere, Nibbler!
Hey, hey! We can all fight when we're drunk. Now, listen, why don't we just brew our own beer?

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: You can brew your own beer?
Fry, are you alright?

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: You did it, Fry! You found the winning bottle-cap! We won!
I like you.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: You do? Look, are you going to help or not?
Bender, you can't crash a mob wedding.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: You forget, Leela, I'm Bender, owner of disguise.
You really don't want me to be captain anymore?

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: You got it, genius.
Yep.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: You humans are so scared of a little robot competition you won't even let us on the field.
Not in Space Massachusetts.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: You mean Space-tax-achusetts. No chance, stretch pants! We're gonna fight to legalize it right here!
Ow! I might've liked Zapp Brannigan if he weren't a pompous dimwit who threw me in prison.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: You really are too picky.
No. You have your legacy as a brutal, tyrannical dictator, and that will outlive any monument.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: You really think they'll remember me?
What the hell are we doing? We're all gonna die so this "junkyard Golem" can celebrate Robanukah.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: You vile racist! Haven't my people suffered enough? Now keep drilling for that petroleum oil, you selfish cowards! Although, then again, I guess any kind of oil would be just as-
It's not the year 4000.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: You were only frozen for two days. Uh, by the way, I broke your bed.
That's great.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: You're moving in with her? Why can't she move in with us? I could just curl up at the foot of the bed.
We're trying our best.

dialogue.speaker: Bender
dialogue.text: Your best is an idiot. Let's pick it up, people. So far it's been crap after crap! I croaked, now show me some love!
